title: Left bundle branch block
summary: The left bundle branch does not conduct. The left ventricle is activated late, cell to cell, and the QRS is wide.

events.label: Normal until the His bundle
events.caption: The atria, the AV node and the His bundle work normally.
events.ecg: A normal P wave and PR interval.

events.label: Right bundle conducts
events.caption: The impulse goes down the right bundle branch and activates the right ventricle first. The left bundle branch is blocked.

events.label: Left ventricle late
events.caption: The impulse has to cross the septum and spread through left ventricular muscle cell to cell, which is slow. The left ventricle is activated late.
events.ecg: The QRS is wide with a broad, notched R wave.

events.label: Wide QRS
events.caption: Activation finishes much later than normal. The abnormal sequence also changes repolarisation.
events.ecg: QRS over 120 ms with an opposite (inverted) T wave.

teaching_points: Left bundle branch block: the QRS is wide and the left ventricle is activated late (slide 91).
A new LBBB can signal significant heart disease; the abnormal activation also hampers coordinated contraction.
A wide-complex tachycardia in a patient with known LBBB may be SVT with aberrancy (slide 93).
